records.source: אָ֣ז יַקְהֵ֣ל שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אֶת־זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל אֶת־כָּל־רָאשֵׁ֣י הַמַּטּוֹת֩ נְשִׂיאֵ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת לִבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְֽהַעֲל֞וֹת אֶת־אֲר֧וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֛ה מֵעִ֥יר דָּוִ֖ד הִ֥יא צִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Then assembled Solomon [the] elders of Israel, all [the] heads of the tribes, [the] leaders of the fathers of [the] sons of Israel, to the king Solomon [in] Jerusalem, to bring up [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh from [the] city of David, that [is] Zion.
pieces: Then Solomon called together the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes and the leaders of the ancestral families of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, to come to King Solomon in Jerusalem. They were to bring the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up from the city of David, that is, Zion.

L.1: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, to King Solomon [in] Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the city of David, which [is] Zion.

R.1: Then King Solomon called the leaders of Israel to come to him in Jerusalem. These were the elders, the heads of all the tribes, and the leaders of the families of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They were to bring the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up to the temple from the city of David, which is also called Zion.

decisions.choice: bring up the ark from the city of David: carry it from David's city up to the new house on the higher ground
decisions.reason: David had brought the ark into his city and set it in a tent he pitched for it (2 Samuel 6:12-17). The temple stood on the hill just north of the old city, at the place David had bought from Araunah (2 Samuel 24:18-25), so the ark goes "up".

decisions.choice: Zion: here the old fortress city of David
decisions.reason: Zion first named the stronghold David captured from the Jebusites (2 Samuel 5:7). Later the name was used for the temple hill and for all Jerusalem, but here it is explained as the city of David, the older part below the temple.

decisions.choice: the leaders of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" is short for "houses of the fathers", the family groups within each tribe (Numbers 1:2; 7:2).

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text of verses 1-5 is followed
decisions.reason: The Greek translation tells verses 1-5 more briefly. It opens by dating the gathering to when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and his own house, and it lacks some of the titles of the leaders and several phrases in the next verses. The longer Hebrew text is kept here.

decisions.choice: up to the temple; also called Zion (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says where the ark was going, which the next verses make clear, and explains that Zion is another name for the city of David.

records.heading: The ark is brought into the temple

records.source: וַיִּקָּ֨הֲל֜וּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּיֶ֥רַח הָאֵֽתָנִ֖ים בֶּחָ֑ג ה֖וּא הַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃
records.gloss: And assembled to the king Solomon all [the] men of Israel in [the] month of Ethanim, at the festival, that [is] the month the seventh.
pieces: All the men of Israel gathered before King Solomon at the festival in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.

L.2: And all the men of Israel assembled to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, at the festival; that [is] the seventh month.

R.2: At the time of the Festival of Booths, all the men of Israel came to King Solomon. This was in the month of Ethanim, the seventh month of the year.

decisions.choice: Ethanim: an older name for the seventh month, around September and October
decisions.reason: Like Ziv and Bul (6:1, 38), Ethanim is one of the old names for the months that Kings uses. The name probably means "ever-flowing", the month when only the streams that never dry up are still running, just before the autumn rains. After the exile the month was called Tishri. The year was counted from the spring (Exodus 12:2), so the seventh month falls in early autumn.

decisions.choice: the festival: the Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: The great pilgrim festival of the seventh month was the Festival of Booths, held for seven days from the fifteenth day of the month (Leviticus 23:34-36; Deuteronomy 16:13-15). "The festival" with the article often means this one (12:32; Nehemiah 8:14).

decisions.choice: the dedication probably came almost a year after the building was finished
alternatives: a month before the work was finished
decisions.reason: The house was finished in the eighth month of Solomon's eleventh year (6:38). The text does not say in which year this seventh month fell; the most natural reading is the following year, eleven months later, so that the dedication could be held at the great autumn festival.

decisions.choice: all the men of Israel: Israel gathered as a people
decisions.reason: The phrase often stands for the nation as a whole (12:1; Judges 20:11). At the pilgrim festivals the men were required to come (Deuteronomy 16:16), though whole families also came (Deuteronomy 16:14).

decisions.choice: the Festival of Booths (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names the festival that the Hebrew calls simply "the festival".

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֶת־הָאָרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And came all [the] elders of Israel, and lifted up the priests the ark.
pieces: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests picked up the ark.

L.3: And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests lifted up the ark.

R.3: When all the elders of Israel had come, the priests lifted the ark onto their shoulders.

decisions.choice: the priests lifted up the ark: carried it by its poles, as the law required
decisions.reason: The ark was to be carried on the shoulders by its poles (Numbers 7:9; Deuteronomy 31:9; 1 Chronicles 15:15). David's first attempt to move it on a cart ended in Uzzah's death (2 Samuel 6:3-7). The parallel in 2 Chronicles 5:4 says "the Levites" lifted the ark.

decisions.choice: onto their shoulders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says how the ark was lifted, since it was carried on poles and never pulled on a cart.

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲל֞וּ אֶת־אֲר֤וֹן יְהוָה֙ וְאֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְאֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּאֹ֑הֶל וַיַּעֲל֣וּ אֹתָ֔ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And brought up the ark of Yahweh and [the] tent of meeting and all [the] vessels of the holiness which [were] in the tent; and brought up them the priests and the Levites.
pieces: They brought up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the tent of meeting, and all the holy utensils that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites carried them up.

L.4: And they brought up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the tent of meeting and all the holy vessels that [were] in the tent; and the priests and the Levites brought them up.

R.4: They brought up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the meeting tent, and all the holy objects that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites carried them up.

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting: probably the old tent from the wilderness, which had stood at Gibeon
alternatives: the tent David set up for the ark in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "Tent of meeting" is the name of the tabernacle Moses made. According to 2 Chronicles 1:3 it stood at Gibeon, the great high place where Solomon worshiped (3:4). It may instead be the tent David pitched for the ark in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:17). Either way, the old place of worship is brought into the new house and stored there.

decisions.choice: the holy vessels: the utensils used in worship
decisions.reason: The word covers all the equipment of the sanctuary, such as bowls, dishes and lampstands (Numbers 3:31; 4:15).

decisions.choice: the priests and the Levites: the priests together with the Levites who helped them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the two groups with "and". The priests carried the ark (verse 3), and the Levites, whose work was to carry the tent and its things (Numbers 4), helped with the rest. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 5:5 reads "the Levitical priests".

decisions.choice: the meeting tent; holy objects (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer "meeting tent" as elsewhere, and "objects" for a word that means any vessel or piece of equipment.

records.source: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְכָל־עֲדַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַנּוֹעָדִ֣ים עָלָ֔יו אִתּ֖וֹ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאָר֑וֹן מְזַבְּחִים֙ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יִסָּפְר֛וּ וְלֹ֥א יִמָּנ֖וּ מֵרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And the king Solomon and all [the] congregation of Israel, those gathered to him, with him before the ark, [were] sacrificing sheep and cattle that not were counted and not were numbered from abundance.
pieces: King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had gathered with him were in front of the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be counted or numbered.

L.5: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered to him [were] with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for abundance.

R.5: King Solomon and the whole community of Israel that had come together were with him in front of the ark. They sacrificed so many sheep and cattle that no one could count them.

decisions.choice: sacrificing: offering sacrifices as the ark was moved
decisions.reason: When David brought the ark into his city, sacrifices were offered along the way (2 Samuel 6:13). Here the whole gathering does the same on a vast scale.

decisions.choice: not counted and not numbered: far too many to count
decisions.reason: The two verbs say the same thing twice for emphasis, as in 3:8.

decisions.choice: community (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses "community" for the congregation, as in the books before.

records.source: וַיָּבִ֣אוּ הַ֠כֹּהֲנִים אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֧ה אֶל־מְקוֹמ֛וֹ אֶל־דְּבִ֥יר הַבַּ֖יִת אֶל־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים אֶל־תַּ֖חַת כַּנְפֵ֥י הַכְּרוּבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And brought the priests [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh to its place, to [the] inner sanctuary of the house, to [the] holy of the holies, to under [the] wings of the cherubim.
pieces: The priests then carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} into its place in the inner sanctuary of the house, the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim.

L.6: And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to its place, into the inner room of the house, into the holy of holies, under the wings of the cherubim.

R.6: The priests carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the place prepared for it. They took it into the inner room of the temple, the most holy place, and set it under the wings of the cherubim.

decisions.choice: the inner sanctuary: the innermost room at the back of the house
decisions.reason: This is the room Solomon built inside the house for the ark, a cube twenty cubits each way, also called the most holy place (6:16, 19-20).

decisions.choice: holy of holies: the most holy place
decisions.reason: Hebrew makes a superlative by joining a noun to its own plural: "the holy of holies" is the holiest place of all, as in the tabernacle (Exodus 26:33-34).

decisions.choice: the cherubim: the two great winged figures Solomon set in the inner room
decisions.reason: These are the two cherubim of olive wood overlaid with gold, ten cubits high, whose wings reached from wall to wall (6:23-28). They are not the two small cherubim on the ark's cover (Exodus 25:18-20).

decisions.choice: house (Literal, Balanced); temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in 1 Kings, Literal and Balanced keep "house" and Readable says "temple". Literal and Readable call the room "the inner room" and Balanced "the inner sanctuary", as in chapter 6.

records.source: כִּ֤י הַכְּרוּבִים֙ פֹּרְשִׂ֣ים כְּנָפַ֔יִם אֶל־מְק֖וֹם הָֽאָר֑וֹן וַיָּסֹ֧כּוּ הַכְּרֻבִ֛ים עַל־הָאָר֥וֹן וְעַל־בַּדָּ֖יו מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: For the cherubim [were] spreading wings to [the] place of the ark, and covered the cherubim over the ark and over its poles from above.
pieces: The cherubim spread their wings over the place where the ark stood, and so the cherubim formed a covering above the ark and its poles.

L.7: For the cherubim were spreading [their] wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim made a covering over the ark and over its poles from above.

R.7: The wings of the cherubim were spread out over the place where the ark was. So their wings formed a cover over the ark and the poles used to carry it.

decisions.choice: its poles: the carrying poles fixed in rings on the sides of the ark
decisions.reason: The poles were to stay in their rings and never be taken out (Exodus 25:13-15).

decisions.choice: covered: screened, sheltered from above
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the cherubim on the ark's cover, whose wings screen it (Exodus 25:20).

decisions.choice: the poles used to carry it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the poles were for.

records.source: וַֽיַּאֲרִכוּ֮ הַבַּדִּים֒ וַיֵּרָאוּ֩ רָאשֵׁ֨י הַבַּדִּ֤ים מִן־הַקֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַדְּבִ֔יר וְלֹ֥א יֵרָא֖וּ הַח֑וּצָה וַיִּ֣הְיוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And were long the poles, and were seen [the] heads of the poles from the holy [place] on [the] face of the inner sanctuary, and not were seen outside; and they are there until the day the this.
pieces: The poles were so long that from the holy place, in front of the inner sanctuary, their ends were visible, though not from outside. They are still there to this day.

L.8: And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the holy [place] in front of the inner room, but they were not seen outside; and they are there to this day.

R.8: The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the holy place, the room in front of the inner room. But no one outside could see them. They are still there to this day.

decisions.choice: the holy place: the main hall of the house, in front of the inner sanctuary
decisions.reason: The house had two rooms: the main hall and, behind it, the inner sanctuary (6:16-17). The ends of the poles could be seen from the hall, but not from the porch or the courtyard.

decisions.choice: to this day: the day of the writer
decisions.reason: This is the first time 1 Kings uses the phrase, which means the time when the account was written. The temple and the ark were lost when the Babylonians burned Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:9), so this remark must come from a source written while the temple still stood, and the writer kept its wording.

decisions.choice: to this day
decisions.reason: Kept at every level, as throughout Samuel, Kings and Chronicles.

records.source: אֵ֚ין בָּֽאָר֔וֹן רַ֗ק שְׁנֵי֙ לֻח֣וֹת הָאֲבָנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִנִּ֥חַ שָׁ֛ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּחֹרֵ֑ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ עִם־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Nothing [was] in the ark only two tablets of the stones which placed there Moses at Horeb, where made Yahweh with [the] sons of Israel in their coming out from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: The ark held nothing but the two stone tablets Moses had put in it at Horeb, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} after they came out of the land of Egypt.

L.9: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made [a covenant] with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt.

R.9: The only things inside the ark were the two stone tablets that Moses had put there at Mount Horeb. That was where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} after they came out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: made [a covenant]: "covenant" is understood
decisions.reason: The verb means "cut" and is the regular verb for making a covenant. Here the word "covenant" is left unsaid, as in 1 Samuel 20:16, but the tablets were the covenant's written terms (Deuteronomy 9:9-11). The parallel in 2 Chronicles 5:10 is worded the same way.

decisions.choice: the two tablets Moses placed there: the tablets of the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: Moses put the second pair of tablets in the ark (Deuteronomy 10:1-5; Exodus 40:20). Other things once kept with the ark, such as the jar of manna (Exodus 16:33-34) and Aaron's staff (Numbers 17:25), are not mentioned.

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy uses Horeb for the mountain where the covenant was made (Deuteronomy 5:2), which Exodus usually calls Sinai.

decisions.choice: Mount Horeb (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Mount" so that the name is not taken for a town.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י בְּצֵ֥את הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים מִן־הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וְהֶעָנָ֥ן מָלֵ֖א אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was, in [the] coming out of the priests from the holy [place], and the cloud filled [the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: As the priests were coming out of the holy place, the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was filled by the cloud.

L.10: And it happened, when the priests came out from the holy [place], that the cloud filled the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: As soon as the priests came out of the holy place, the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was filled with the cloud.

decisions.choice: the cloud filled the house: as it once covered the tabernacle
decisions.reason: When the tabernacle was finished, the cloud covered the tent of meeting and the glory of Yahweh filled it (Exodus 40:34). The same cloud now fills the house Solomon has built. The article points to the known cloud of Yahweh's presence that led Israel from Egypt (Exodus 13:21-22).

decisions.choice: the holy place: the sanctuary where they had set the ark
decisions.reason: The priests had gone into the inner sanctuary to set the ark in place (verse 6). "The holy" can name the whole sanctuary or its inner room; the point is that they had come out when the cloud came.

decisions.choice: the parallel in Chronicles adds the singers
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 5:11-14 tells that when the priests came out, the Levite singers and trumpeters praised Yahweh, "for he is good, for his steadfast love is forever", and then the house was filled with the cloud.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים לַעֲמֹ֥ד לְשָׁרֵ֖ת מִפְּנֵ֥י הֶֽעָנָ֑ן כִּי־מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And not were able the priests to stand to minister because of the cloud, for filled [the] glory of Yahweh [the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: The priests were unable to stand and do their service because of the cloud, since the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was full of the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.11: And the priests were not able to stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: The priests could not stand there to do their work because of the cloud. The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} filled the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: not able ... for the glory filled the house: as at the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Exodus 40:35 says that Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle. The same words are used here of the priests and the house. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 5:14 has the same sentence, and 2 Chronicles 7:1-2 tells of the glory filling the house again after the prayer.

decisions.choice: the glory of Yahweh: his presence made visible
decisions.reason: The glory is Yahweh himself present among his people. By filling the house he shows that he accepts it as his dwelling, as Solomon's words in the next verses say.

decisions.choice: to stand to minister: to stay at their posts and serve
decisions.reason: Priests "stand before Yahweh to minister" (Deuteronomy 10:8; 18:5). The cloud made it impossible to remain in their place.

decisions.choice: the house was full of the glory (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the wording of Exodus 40:35, where the same sentence is used of the tabernacle.

records.source: אָ֖ז אָמַ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה יְהוָ֣ה אָמַ֔ר לִשְׁכֹּ֖ן בָּעֲרָפֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Then said Solomon, Yahweh said to dwell in the thick darkness.
pieces: Then Solomon said, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would dwell in thick darkness.

L.12: Then Solomon said, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said [that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would] dwell in thick darkness.

R.12: Then Solomon said, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would live in a thick, dark cloud.

decisions.choice: has said to dwell: has said that he would dwell
decisions.reason: The verb "dwell" is an infinitive after "said". It reports what Yahweh had said about himself; "said" can also mean "decided".

decisions.choice: thick darkness: the dark cloud of Yahweh's presence
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses drew near to "the thick darkness where God was" (Exodus 20:21; Deuteronomy 4:11; 5:22), and Yahweh appeared in the cloud over the ark's cover (Leviticus 16:2). The cloud that has just filled the house is that darkness: Yahweh is truly present, yet hidden.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text and its place are kept
alternatives: add the Greek line about the sun and the reference to a book of songs
decisions.reason: In the Greek translation these words come after verse 53, in a longer form that begins with a line about the sun in the heavens and ends by saying that the words are written "in the book of the song". The Hebrew words for "the song" (*hashir*) and "the upright" (*hayashar*) use the same letters in a different order, so the source may be the Book of Jashar quoted in Joshua 10:13 and 2 Samuel 1:18. The Greek may keep an older, fuller form of the poem, or it may expand it; the evidence is not clear. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 6:1-2 agrees with the Hebrew of Kings.

decisions.choice: live in a thick, dark cloud (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "live" for "dwell" and describes the thick darkness as a dark cloud, linking it with the cloud of verses 10-11.

records.heading: Solomon speaks to the people

records.source: בָּנֹ֥ה בָנִ֛יתִי בֵּ֥ית זְבֻ֖ל לָ֑ךְ מָכ֥וֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ֖ עוֹלָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: Surely I have built a house of loftiness for you, a place for your dwelling forever.
pieces: I have indeed built a lofty house for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q a place for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to dwell forever."

L.13: I have surely built an exalted house for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q a place for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dwelling forever."

R.13: Now I have built a magnificent temple for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q a place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can live forever."

decisions.choice: a house of loftiness: an exalted, royal dwelling
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It is used of God's "holy and glorious dwelling" in heaven (Isaiah 63:15) and of the dwelling of the sun and moon (Habakkuk 3:11). In related languages it is a title meaning "prince", so the house is a dwelling fit for a king.

decisions.choice: a place for your dwelling: as Moses sang at the sea
decisions.reason: The same words are used in the Song of the Sea: "the place for your dwelling that you have made, Yahweh, the sanctuary" (Exodus 15:17). The word for "place" means a fixed, established place. Solomon sees the house as the fulfillment of that promise. 2 Chronicles 6:2 has the same line.

decisions.choice: I have surely built ... forever
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. "Forever" is plural in Hebrew, "for ages", meaning for all time.

decisions.choice: magnificent temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the rare word with a common one.

records.source: וַיַּסֵּ֤ב הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת־פָּנָ֔יו וַיְבָ֕רֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכָל־קְהַ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹמֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And turned the king his face and blessed all [the] assembly of Israel, and all [the] assembly of Israel [was] standing.
pieces: Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood there.

L.14: And the king turned his face around and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel [was] standing.

R.14: Then the king turned around to face all the people of Israel who were gathered there. They were all standing, and he blessed them.

decisions.choice: turned his face: from facing the house to facing the people
decisions.reason: Solomon had spoken his words about the house toward the sanctuary (verses 12-13). Now he turns to the people gathered in the courtyard.

decisions.choice: blessed: spoke words of blessing over them
decisions.reason: To bless the people is to ask God's good for them. The words that follow begin by blessing Yahweh (verse 15), praising him for what he has done for them.

decisions.choice: assembly: Israel gathered for worship
decisions.reason: The word is used of Israel called together before Yahweh, as at Sinai (Deuteronomy 9:10; 18:16).

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel who were gathered there (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "assembly" as the people who had gathered.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר בְּפִ֔יו אֵ֖ת דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י וּבְיָד֥וֹ מִלֵּ֖א לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And he said, Blessed [be] Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth with David my father, and with his hand has fulfilled, saying,
pieces: He said, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own mouth made a promise to my father David and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own hand has now fulfilled it. For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said,

L.15: And he said, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who spoke with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth to David my father, and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand has fulfilled [it], saying,

R.15: He said, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel! He made a promise to my father David, and now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised. This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said:

decisions.choice: blessed be: praised and thanked
decisions.reason: When people bless God, they praise him and give him thanks for what he has done (Genesis 24:27; Exodus 18:10).

decisions.choice: with his mouth ... with his hand: what Yahweh said, he has now done
decisions.reason: The mouth that spoke the promise and the hand that carried it out belong to the same God. Solomon says it again in verse 24.

decisions.choice: spoke to David my father: the promise through Nathan
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised David that his son would build a house for his name (2 Samuel 7:12-13).

decisions.choice: Praise (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "Praise" because "bless" said of God is not familiar to many readers.

records.source: מִן־הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצֵ֜אתִי אֶת־עַמִּ֣י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ מִמִּצְרַיִם֒ לֹֽא־בָחַ֣רְתִּי בְעִ֗יר מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לִהְי֥וֹת שְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑ם וָאֶבְחַ֣ר בְּדָוִ֔ד לִֽהְי֖וֹת עַל־עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: From the day that I brought out my people Israel from Egypt, not I chose a city from all [the] tribes of Israel to build a house for being my name there; and I chose David to be over my people Israel.
pieces: 'Since the day I brought {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel out of Egypt, I have chosen no city in any tribe of Israel in which to build a house where {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name would be. But I chose David to rule over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

L.16: 'From the day that I brought {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to be there; but I have chosen David to be over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

R.16: 'I have not chosen any city in all the tribes of Israel as the place to build a temple for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, not since I brought {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel out of Egypt. But I chose David to rule over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

decisions.choice: for my name to be there: for a house that bears Yahweh's name and is the place where he is known and called on
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy speaks of the place Yahweh would choose "to put his name there" and "to make his name dwell there" (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11). His name is Yahweh himself as he has made himself known. Where his name is, he is truly present to hear his people (verses 29-30), yet Solomon also says that even the highest heaven cannot contain him (verse 27), and he asks Yahweh to hear "in heaven". The house belongs to him and bears his name (verse 43).

decisions.choice: the shorter Hebrew text of Kings is kept
alternatives: add "but I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there"
decisions.reason: The parallel in 2 Chronicles 6:5-6 is longer: "... nor did I choose anyone to be ruler over my people Israel; but I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel." The Greek translation of Kings also has the words about choosing Jerusalem. The shorter Hebrew may have lost a line when a copyist's eye skipped between two similar phrases. Either way the meaning is the same: Yahweh chose both the city and the king.

decisions.choice: to be over my people: to rule them
decisions.reason: To be "over" a people is to be their ruler (2 Samuel 7:8).

decisions.choice: house (Literal, Balanced); temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י עִם־לְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And it was with [the] heart of David my father to build a house for [the] name of Yahweh, [the] God of Israel.
pieces: My father David had it in his heart to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.17: And it was with the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

R.17: My father David wanted to build a temple for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: it was with the heart of David: David intended and longed to do it
decisions.reason: The heart is where plans are made. David told Nathan that he wanted to build a house for the ark (2 Samuel 7:1-3).

decisions.choice: wanted (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the heart idiom in plain words.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָיָה֙ עִם־לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י הֱטִיבֹ֔תָ כִּ֥י הָיָ֖ה עִם־לְבָבֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to David my father, Because that it was with your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was with your heart.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to my father David, 'You wanted to build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and you did well to have this in your heart.

L.18: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to David my father, 'Because it was with your heart to build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, you did well that it was with your heart.

R.18: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to my father David, 'You wanted to build a temple for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. It was good that you wanted to do this.

decisions.choice: you did well: Yahweh approves David's desire even though he does not let him carry it out
decisions.reason: These words are not found in 2 Samuel 7, though they agree with it: Yahweh honors what David wanted, and gives the task to his son.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The "and" that joins the two verses points to a contrast: David wanted to build, but Yahweh said otherwise.

records.source: רַ֣ק אַתָּ֔ה לֹ֥א תִבְנֶ֖ה הַבָּ֑יִת כִּ֤י אִם־בִּנְךָ֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣א מֵחֲלָצֶ֔יךָ הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה הַבַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִֽי׃
records.gloss: Only you not will build the house, but your son, the one coming out from your loins, he will build the house for my name.
pieces: Yet you are not the one who will build the house. Your son, your own offspring, is the one who will build the house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

L.19: Only, you will not build the house; but your son, who will come out of your loins, he will build the house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

R.19: But you will not be the one to build it. Your own son will build the temple for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

decisions.choice: who will come out of your loins: your own son
decisions.reason: The loins stand for the body as the source of children (Genesis 35:11). The words echo the promise in 2 Samuel 7:12.

decisions.choice: you will not build the house
decisions.reason: The reason is given elsewhere: David was kept busy by the wars around him (5:17), and he had shed much blood (1 Chronicles 22:8).

decisions.choice: your own offspring (Balanced); your own son (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the picture of the loins in plain words.

records.source: וַיָּ֣קֶם יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־דְּבָר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר וָאָקֻ֡ם תַּחַת֩ דָּוִ֨ד אָבִ֜י וָאֵשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וָאֶבְנֶ֣ה הַבַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And established Yahweh his word that he spoke, and I have risen in place of David my father, and I sit on [the] throne of Israel as spoke Yahweh, and I have built the house for [the] name of Yahweh, [the] God of Israel.
pieces: Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has kept the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made. I have taken the place of my father David and sit on Israel's throne, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised, and I have built this house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.20: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has established {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke; and I have risen in place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke; and I have built the house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

R.20: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise. I have become king after my father David, and I sit on the throne of Israel, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised. And I have built the temple for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: established his word: made his promise stand, kept it
decisions.reason: The verb means "make stand". A word that is made to stand is one that comes true (2:4; 6:12).

decisions.choice: I have risen in place of David: I have become king after him
decisions.reason: To "rise" in someone's place is to succeed him (Deuteronomy 29:21).

decisions.choice: promise; promised (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Word" and "spoke" here mean the promise Yahweh made, so Balanced and Readable say "promise".

records.source: וָאָשִׂ֨ם שָׁ֤ם מָקוֹם֙ לָֽאָר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּרַת֙ עִם־אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ בְּהוֹצִיא֥וֹ אֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: And I have set there a place for the ark, where there [is] [the] covenant of Yahweh that he made with our fathers when he brought them out from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: There I have prepared a place for the ark, which holds the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with our ancestors when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out of the land of Egypt."

L.21: And I have set there a place for the ark, in which [is] the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with our fathers when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out of the land of Egypt."

R.21: In the temple I have made a place for the ark. Inside the ark is the covenant {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made with our ancestors when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out of Egypt."

decisions.choice: the covenant: the stone tablets on which the covenant was written
decisions.reason: What is in the ark is the two tablets (verse 9), called "the tablets of the covenant" (Deuteronomy 9:9). The covenant is named for the tablets that record it.

decisions.choice: fathers (Literal); ancestors (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means forefathers, the generation of the exodus.

records.source: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִפְנֵי֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה נֶ֖גֶד כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And stood Solomon before [the] altar of Yahweh in front of all [the] assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms [to] the heavens.
pieces: Then Solomon took his place before the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven.

L.22: And Solomon stood before the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms [toward] the heavens.

R.22: Then Solomon stood in front of the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with all the people of Israel there. He held up his open hands toward heaven to pray.

decisions.choice: spread out his palms toward heaven: the posture of prayer
decisions.reason: People prayed standing or kneeling with open hands lifted up (Exodus 9:29; Isaiah 1:15). Verse 54 says that Solomon ended the prayer on his knees.

decisions.choice: the altar of Yahweh: the great bronze altar in the courtyard
decisions.reason: This is the altar for burnt offerings in front of the house (verse 64). The parallel in 2 Chronicles 6:12-13 adds that Solomon stood on a bronze platform in the courtyard and knelt there.

decisions.choice: to pray (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture meant, since the prayer follows at once.

records.heading: Solomon's prayer of dedication

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֵין־כָּמ֣וֹךָ אֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם מִמַּ֔עַל וְעַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ מִתָּ֑חַת שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וְֽהַחֶ֔סֶד לַעֲבָדֶ֕יךָ הַהֹלְכִ֥ים לְפָנֶ֖יךָ בְּכָל־לִבָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said, Yahweh, God of Israel, there is no like you God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath, keeping the covenant and the steadfast love for your servants who walk before you with all their heart,
pieces: He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, there is no God like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the heavens above or on the earth beneath. You keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant and show faithful love to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants who walk before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all their heart,

L.23: And he said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, there is no God like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the heavens above or on the earth beneath, keeping the covenant and the steadfast love for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves who walk before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all their heart,

R.23: Solomon prayed, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, there is no God like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} anywhere, in the sky above or on the earth below. You keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant and show faithful love to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants who live for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all their heart.

decisions.choice: there is no God like you: Yahweh has no equal
decisions.reason: Israel confessed that no god could be compared with Yahweh, in heaven or on earth (Exodus 15:11; Deuteronomy 4:39).

decisions.choice: keeping the covenant and the steadfast love: faithful to the covenant and to the love it promises
decisions.reason: The same words describe Yahweh in Deuteronomy 7:9, 12. The word for steadfast love (*chesed*) is the loyal, generous love that keeps its commitments. Here the two nouns belong together: Yahweh keeps his covenant by showing steadfast love.

decisions.choice: walk before you: live in your sight, serving you
decisions.reason: To walk before Yahweh is to live one's whole life aware of him and obeying him (Genesis 17:1; 1 Kings 2:4).

decisions.choice: steadfast love, slaves (Literal); faithful love, servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *Chesed* is "steadfast love" at Literal and "faithful love" at Balanced and Readable, as in 3:6. Those who serve God are his "slaves" at Literal and "servants" at the other levels, following the rule for *'eved*.

decisions.choice: Solomon prayed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and says that what follows is a prayer, after the speech to the people in verses 15-21.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֗רְתָּ לְעַבְדְּךָ֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ ל֑וֹ וַתְּדַבֵּ֥ר בְּפִ֛יךָ וּבְיָדְךָ֥ מִלֵּ֖אתָ כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: who have kept for your servant David my father what you spoke to him; and you spoke with your mouth, and with your hand you have fulfilled, as the day the this.
pieces: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who have kept for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, my father David, the promise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made to him. With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mouth {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised, and with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have fulfilled it, as it is today.

L.24: who have kept for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave David my father what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke to him; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mouth, and with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have fulfilled [it], as [it is] this day.

R.24: You have kept the promise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, my father David. What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mouth, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, as we see today.

decisions.choice: with your mouth ... with your hand: what you promised you have done
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

decisions.choice: as this day: as can be seen today
decisions.reason: The finished house standing before them is the proof that the promise has been kept.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23. David is Yahweh's servant in the honored sense of one who belongs to him and serves him.

L.25: And now, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, keep for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave David my father what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke to him, saying, 'There shall not be cut off for you a man from before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sitting on the throne of Israel, if only your sons keep their way, to walk before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as you have walked before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

R.25: Now, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, keep the promise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, my father David. You told him, 'If your descendants are careful to live for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as you have done, one of your family will always sit on the throne of Israel before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: a man will not be cut off for you: you will never lack a descendant on the throne
decisions.reason: The same promise is quoted in 2:4 and again in 9:5. It goes back to 2 Samuel 7:12-16.

decisions.choice: only if: the promise is joined to a condition
decisions.reason: Yahweh's promise to David stands, but each king's place on the throne depends on walking before Yahweh. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 6:16 says "to walk in my law" for "to walk before me".

decisions.choice: keep their way: watch how they live
decisions.reason: "Way" means a person's conduct.

decisions.choice: slave, sons (Literal); servant, descendants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23 for "slave". "Sons" here means all of David's line, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

pieces: But will God really live on earth? Heaven itself, even the highest heaven, cannot contain {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. How much less this house that I have built!

L.27: But will God truly dwell on the earth? Look, the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; how much less this house that I have built!

R.27: But can God really live on earth? Even the sky and the highest heaven cannot hold {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. So this temple I have built certainly cannot hold {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

decisions.choice: God is not confined to the house
decisions.reason: Solomon has just said that he built a place for Yahweh to dwell forever (verse 13). Now he says that no place can contain him. The house is where Yahweh chooses to put his name and to hear prayer (verses 29-30), while he himself dwells in heaven.

decisions.choice: the heavens of the heavens: the highest heaven
decisions.reason: This is a superlative, like "holy of holies" (verse 6), as in Deuteronomy 10:14 and Psalm 148:4.

decisions.choice: dwell on the earth
decisions.reason: The parallel in 2 Chronicles 6:18 reads "dwell with humankind on the earth".

decisions.choice: certainly cannot hold you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable completes the comparison "how much less" in plain words.

L.28: Yet turn to the prayer of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and to his plea, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant is praying before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} today,

decisions.choice: prayer, plea, cry: three words for asking God
decisions.reason: The first is the general word for prayer. The second (*techinnah*) is a plea for favor or mercy. The third (*rinnah*) is a loud cry, often of joy, here of urgent asking.

decisions.choice: turn to: give attention to
decisions.reason: To turn toward a prayer is to take notice of it and respond (Psalm 102:18).

decisions.choice: your servant (all levels); me, I (Readable)
decisions.reason: Solomon speaks of himself politely as "your servant". The words stay "your servant" at every level, as in 3:7; Readable also says "me" and "I" so that it is clear Solomon means himself.

pieces: so that night and day {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes may be open toward this house, toward the place about which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said, 'My name will be there.' Listen to the prayer that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant prays toward this place.

L.29: that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes may be open toward this house night and day, toward the place of which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said, 'My name shall be there,' to listen to the prayer that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant prays toward this place.

R.29: Watch over this temple night and day. You said that this is the place where {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name would be. So listen when I, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, pray toward this place.

decisions.choice: your eyes open: watching over it with care
decisions.reason: Yahweh's eyes are on the land he cares for (Deuteronomy 11:12), and here on the house and those who pray there.

decisions.choice: My name will be there
decisions.reason: See verse 16. Yahweh is in heaven (verse 30), but his name is in the house, so that prayer made there or toward it reaches him.

decisions.choice: toward this place: praying while facing the house, even from far away
decisions.reason: The prayer expects people to pray toward the house when they cannot come to it (verses 35, 38, 44, 48). Daniel prayed in Babylon with his windows open toward Jerusalem (Daniel 6:11).

decisions.choice: your servant (all levels); I (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

pieces: Listen to the pleading of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel as they pray toward this place. Hear in heaven, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dwelling place; and when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear, forgive.

L.30: And listen to the plea of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel when they pray toward this place; and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, hear in the place of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dwelling, in the heavens; and hear and forgive.

R.30: Listen when I, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel ask for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help as we pray toward this place. Listen from heaven, where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} live. And when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear, forgive.

decisions.choice: hear in heaven, your dwelling place: Yahweh hears from heaven the prayers made toward the house
decisions.reason: This is the refrain of the prayer (verses 32, 34, 36, 39, 43, 45, 49). The house is the place toward which prayer is made; heaven is where Yahweh dwells and from where he answers.

decisions.choice: forgive: pardon and restore
decisions.reason: In the Bible this verb always has God as its subject. Forgiveness is the main thing Solomon asks for in the cases that follow.

decisions.choice: they pray: the people pray
decisions.reason: The plural verb refers to the people of Israel. The king and the people pray together toward the house.

decisions.choice: hear in heaven, your dwelling place, and forgive
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded the same way each time it returns. Literal has "hear [in] the heavens, the place of your dwelling", Balanced "hear in heaven, your dwelling place", and Readable "listen from heaven, where you live". Here the Hebrew has "to" ("to the place ... to the heavens"), which Literal renders "in".

decisions.choice: your servant (all levels); I (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

records.gloss: [In the case] that sins a man against his neighbor, and he lays on him an oath to make him swear, and comes [the] oath before your altar in the house the this,
pieces: When someone sins against a neighbor and is required to take an oath, and comes and swears the oath before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar in this house,

L.31: If a man sins against his neighbor, and he lays an oath on him to make him swear, and the oath comes before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar in this house,

R.31: Suppose someone is accused of wronging a neighbor and is made to swear an oath that he is innocent. If he comes and takes this oath in front of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar in this temple,

decisions.choice: an oath to make him swear: an oath calling down a curse on himself if he is guilty
decisions.reason: When a wrong could not be proved by witnesses, the accused person swore before Yahweh that he was innocent, accepting a curse if he lied (Exodus 22:6-10; Numbers 5:19-22). Yahweh himself was then left to judge.

decisions.choice: he lays an oath on him: the one wronged, or the judges, require the oath
alternatives: the accused takes the oath on himself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name who lays the oath on the accused. It is probably the neighbor who brings the charge, or the judges who hear the case.

decisions.choice: accused of; that he is innocent (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the situation: the wrong has not been proved, and the oath is a claim of innocence that only God can test.

pieces: then hear in heaven and act. Judge between {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants: condemn the guilty by bringing on his own head what he has done, and declare the innocent in the right by rewarding him for his righteousness.

L.32: then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, hear [in] the heavens, and act, and judge {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves, condemning the guilty by bringing his way on his own head, and justifying the righteous by giving to him according to his righteousness.

R.32: then listen from heaven and act. Judge between {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants. Punish the guilty one for what he has done, and show that the innocent one is right by rewarding him for his righteousness.

decisions.choice: condemn the guilty, justify the righteous: declare each one guilty or innocent
decisions.reason: These are words of the law court. A judge was to declare the innocent in the right and the guilty in the wrong (Deuteronomy 25:1). Solomon asks Yahweh to do this where human judges cannot know the truth.

decisions.choice: bringing his way on his head: making his own conduct fall back on him
decisions.reason: The guilty person bears the results of what he has done, as in 2:32-33.

decisions.choice: hear in heaven
decisions.reason: As in verse 30: the refrain keeps one wording at each level.

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

R.33: Suppose {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel are beaten by an enemy because they have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. If they then turn back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and pray to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in this temple, asking for mercy,

decisions.choice: defeat because of sin
decisions.reason: The covenant warned that if Israel turned from Yahweh they would be struck down before their enemies (Leviticus 26:17; Deuteronomy 28:25). Solomon asks for mercy when that happens.

decisions.choice: confess your name: acknowledge Yahweh, praising him and admitting that he is just
decisions.reason: The verb means to acknowledge, give thanks or confess. Turning back to Yahweh includes owning that he was right to punish (Joshua 7:19).

decisions.choice: turn back: repent
decisions.reason: The verb "turn" or "return" is the main word for repentance in the Old Testament (Deuteronomy 30:2).

decisions.choice: confess (Literal); acknowledge (Balanced); honor (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps one word for this verb through the prayer (verses 33 and 35).

records.gloss: and you, hear [in] the heavens, and forgive [the] sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that you gave to their fathers.
pieces: then hear in heaven and forgive {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel for their sin, and bring them back to the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to their ancestors.

L.34: then {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, hear [in] the heavens, and forgive the sin of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel, and bring them back to the land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave to their fathers.

R.34: then listen from heaven and forgive the sin of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel. Bring them back to the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave their ancestors.

decisions.choice: bring them back to the land: those taken captive after the defeat
decisions.reason: Defeat in battle often meant that some were carried off as prisoners (Deuteronomy 28:41). Solomon asks that they be brought home.

decisions.choice: hear in heaven and forgive
decisions.reason: As in verse 30: the refrain keeps one wording at each level.

decisions.choice: the heavens shut up: drought sent as a warning
decisions.reason: The covenant warned that Yahweh would shut up the heavens so that there would be no rain if Israel turned to other gods (Deuteronomy 11:17; Leviticus 26:19). The drought in Elijah's day is an example (17:1).

decisions.choice: because you afflict them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels give "because you afflict them": the drought has humbled them and made them turn. The same letters can be read "when you answer them", meaning that they turn from sin when Yahweh answers their prayer. The traditional reading is followed.

decisions.choice: the people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names who has sinned, since the verse does not.

decisions.reason: The little word can mean "when", "for" or "so that". Yahweh forgives as he teaches his people, through the hardship and through his word, the way they should live. The verb "teach" is related to the word *torah*, "instruction".

decisions.choice: blight, mildew: diseases of the grain
decisions.reason: The first word is the scorching of crops by the hot east wind; the second is a disease that turns grain pale or yellow. They appear together among the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:22; Amos 4:9).

decisions.choice: locust, grasshopper: two kinds or stages of locust
decisions.reason: Several Hebrew words name locusts. The second word comes from a verb meaning "consume" and may be a stage of the locust's growth, or another kind of insect that strips the fields.

decisions.choice: in the land of their gates: in their cities
decisions.reason: "Gates" stands for cities, as often (Deuteronomy 12:15). The Hebrew "in the land of its gates" is unusual, and the Greek translation reads "in one of their cities". The parallel in 2 Chronicles 6:28 has the same words as the Hebrew here. The sense is that an enemy besieges one of Israel's towns.

decisions.choice: it ... its enemy: Israel as one people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the nation as "it", one body.

decisions.choice: crops are ruined by hot winds (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the blight by its cause.

decisions.choice: there is no one who does not sin
decisions.reason: Solomon admits that sin is universal, his own people included (Ecclesiastes 7:20; Psalm 143:2). The prayer does not hope that Israel will never sin, but that Yahweh will forgive when they turn back.

decisions.reason: The law warned that unfaithful Israel would be scattered among the nations (Leviticus 26:33-39; Deuteronomy 28:36, 64). Readers after the fall of Jerusalem, when Judah was carried off to Babylon (2 Kings 25:21), would hear their own situation in these verses.

records.source: וְהֵשִׁ֨יבוּ֙ אֶל־לִבָּ֔ם בָּאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבּוּ־שָׁ֑ם וְשָׁ֣בוּ׀וְהִֽתְחַנְּנ֣וּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ שֹֽׁבֵיהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר חָטָ֥אנוּ וְהֶעֱוִ֖ינוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ׃

L.47: and they bring [it] back to their heart in the land where they have been taken captive, and they turn back and plead with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly,'

decisions.choice: bring back to their heart: come to their senses, take it to heart
decisions.reason: The phrase means to think again and see things as they are (Deuteronomy 4:39; 30:1; Lamentations 3:21).

decisions.choice: bring back ... taken captive ... turn back: a play on sounds
decisions.reason: "Turn back" and "take captive" sound alike in Hebrew. Those who were taken captive (*nishbu*) now turn back (*shavu*) to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly
decisions.reason: The three verbs make a full confession. Later generations used the same words (Psalm 106:6; Daniel 9:5), and the parallel in 2 Chronicles 6:37 has them too.

And suppose they pray to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} facing toward their own land, the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave their ancestors, and toward the city {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} chose and the temple I built for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

decisions.choice: return to you with all their heart and all their soul
decisions.reason: Moses promised that if Israel in exile returned to Yahweh with all their heart and soul, he would have mercy and gather them again (Deuteronomy 4:29-31; 30:1-3).

decisions.choice: pray toward their land, the city and the house
decisions.reason: Exiles far from home would pray facing Jerusalem, as Daniel did (Daniel 6:11). The three goals, land, city and house, narrow down to the place where Yahweh's name is.

decisions.reason: This word names a willful breaking away from an authority, like a subject rebelling against a king (2 Kings 1:1).

decisions.choice: give them compassion before their captors: move the captors to pity them
decisions.reason: Yahweh can turn the hearts of those who hold his people captive (Psalm 106:46; Ezra 9:9; Nehemiah 1:11).

decisions.choice: transgressions (Literal); rebellious acts (Balanced); rebelled (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of sin the word means.

R.51: They are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own special possession. You brought them out of Egypt, where their suffering was like the heat of a furnace for melting iron.

decisions.choice: the iron furnace: Egypt as a place of fierce suffering
decisions.reason: A furnace for smelting iron was the hottest fire people knew. Egypt is called the iron furnace in Deuteronomy 4:20 and Jeremiah 11:4.

decisions.choice: your people and your inheritance: as Moses prayed
decisions.reason: Moses pleaded for Israel with the same words: "they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out" (Deuteronomy 9:26, 29). Israel belongs to Yahweh, so Solomon asks him to care for what is his.

decisions.choice: your own special possession; the heat of a furnace for melting iron (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "inheritance" and the picture of the iron furnace.

decisions.choice: your eyes open: watching with care
decisions.reason: As in verse 29.

decisions.choice: your servant (all levels); me (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

records.gloss: For you separated them for yourself as an inheritance from all [the] peoples of the earth, as you spoke by [the] hand of Moses your servant when you brought out our fathers from Egypt, Lord Yahweh.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set them apart from all the peoples of the earth to be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own inheritance, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} declared through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought our ancestors out of Egypt, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}."

L.53: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set them apart for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke by the hand of Moses {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought our fathers out of Egypt, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}."

R.53: You chose them out of all the nations on earth to belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You said this through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Moses when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought our ancestors out of Egypt, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: set them apart for yourself as an inheritance
decisions.reason: Yahweh set Israel apart from the peoples to be his own (Leviticus 20:24, 26, with the same verb; Exodus 19:5-6; Deuteronomy 9:29).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means "through" a messenger (Exodus 9:35).

decisions.choice: the end of the prayer, and the parallel in Chronicles
decisions.reason: In 2 Chronicles 6:40-42 the prayer ends differently, with words from Psalm 132:8-10: "Arise, Yahweh God, to your resting place." In the Greek translation of Kings, Solomon's poem of verses 12-13 follows here (see verse 12).

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable); Lord GOD
decisions.reason: "Moses your servant" follows the rule for *'eved*. The title "my Lord Yahweh" is written "Lord GOD" with the divine name, as everywhere.

pieces: When Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and plea to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, he got up from where he had been kneeling before the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, his hands spread out toward heaven.

L.54: And it happened, when Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and plea to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, he rose from before the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, from kneeling on his knees, with his palms spread out [toward] the heavens.

R.54: When Solomon finished praying this prayer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and asking for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} help, he got up from in front of the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He had been kneeling there with his hands held out toward heaven.

decisions.choice: he rose from kneeling: he had knelt during the prayer
decisions.reason: Verse 22 says he stood to begin the prayer. At some point he knelt, and now he rises. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 6:13 says that he stood on a bronze platform and then knelt.

decisions.choice: when Solomon had finished praying
decisions.reason: At this point 2 Chronicles 7:1-3 tells that fire came down from heaven and consumed the offerings, and the glory of Yahweh filled the house. Kings goes straight on to Solomon's blessing.

decisions.choice: asking for his help (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "plea".

records.heading: Solomon blesses the people

records.source: וַֽיַּעְמֹ֕ד וַיְבָ֕רֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ק֥וֹל גָּד֖וֹל לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And he stood and blessed all [the] assembly of Israel [with] a voice great, saying,

decisions.choice: blessed: spoke a blessing over them
decisions.reason: As in verse 14. Again the blessing begins by praising Yahweh (verse 56) and goes on to ask his good for the people (verses 57-61).

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel who were gathered there (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 14.

records.source: בָּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן מְנוּחָה֙ לְעַמּ֣וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר לֹֽא־נָפַ֞ל דָּבָ֣ר אֶחָ֗ד מִכֹּל֙ דְּבָר֣וֹ הַטּ֔וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

pieces: "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has given rest to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised. Of all the good promises {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Moses, not one word has failed.

L.56: "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has given rest to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel according to all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke. Not one word has fallen of all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} good word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by the hand of Moses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave.

R.56: "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! He has given {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel a place to rest, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised. Every one of the good promises {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Moses has come true.

decisions.choice: who has given rest: peace and safety in the land
decisions.reason: Moses promised that Yahweh would give Israel rest from all their enemies in the land (Deuteronomy 12:9-10). The promise was partly kept in Joshua's day (Joshua 21:43-45) and in David's (2 Samuel 7:1), and now Solomon sees it fully kept, with the house built in the place Yahweh chose.

decisions.choice: not one word has fallen: not one promise has failed
decisions.reason: A word that "falls" is one that comes to nothing. Joshua said the same: "not one word has fallen of all the good words" (Joshua 21:45; 23:14).

decisions.choice: Praise (Readable); slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verses 15 and 53.

records.source: יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ אַל־יַעַזְבֵ֖נוּ וְאַֽל־יִטְּשֵֽׁנוּ׃
records.gloss: May be Yahweh our God with us as he was with our fathers; may he not leave us and not forsake us,
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God be with us just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with our ancestors. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never leave us or abandon us,

L.57: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God be with us as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with our fathers; may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not leave us nor forsake us,

R.57: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God stay with us as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed with our ancestors. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never leave us or give up on us.

decisions.choice: may he not leave us nor forsake us: as Yahweh promised Moses and Joshua
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised, "I will not leave you or forsake you" (Deuteronomy 31:6, 8; Joshua 1:5). Solomon turns the promise into a prayer.

records.gloss: to incline our heart to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments that he commanded our fathers.
pieces: so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may turn our hearts toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and we may walk in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded our ancestors.

decisions.choice: to incline our heart to him: Yahweh himself turns the heart
decisions.reason: Solomon asks Yahweh not only to be with his people but to make them willing to obey. Moses promised that Yahweh would circumcise their hearts so that they would love him (Deuteronomy 30:6).

decisions.choice: commandments, statutes, judgments (Literal); commandments, statutes, rulings (Balanced); commands, laws, rules (Readable)

decisions.reason: The word means complete, at peace, with nothing held back. It sounds like Solomon's own name. Sadly, 11:4 will say that in old age Solomon's heart was not whole with Yahweh his God, and the same measure is used for later kings (15:3, 14).

decisions.reason: Solomon says that the people are now keeping faith, and asks that they continue.

decisions.reason: The dedication is completed with sacrifices on a great scale. The parallel is 2 Chronicles 7:4-5.

pieces: Solomon offered as peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep. In this way the king and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} dedicated the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.63: And Solomon sacrificed the sacrifice of the peace offerings that he sacrificed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep. And the king and all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel dedicated the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.63: Solomon offered 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep as peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This is how the king and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} dedicated the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: peace offerings: sacrifices shared in a meal
decisions.reason: In a peace offering the fat was burned for Yahweh and most of the meat was eaten by the worshipers (Leviticus 3; 7:11-21). So these vast offerings fed the crowd through the days of the festival.

decisions.choice: dedicated: began to use the house for its purpose
decisions.reason: The verb means to open or begin using something new, as a new house (Deuteronomy 20:5). The later Festival of Dedication, Hanukkah, takes its name from this word.

decisions.choice: 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep
decisions.reason: The numbers are very large. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 7:5 has the same figures. Verse 64 explains that a second place had to be made holy to offer them all.

pieces: That same day the king made holy the central part of the courtyard before the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He offered there the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat parts of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that stood before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was too small to hold them: the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings.

L.64: On that day the king consecrated the middle of the court that [was] in front of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for there he offered the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that [was] before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was too small to hold the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings.

R.64: That same day the king set apart the middle of the courtyard in front of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a holy place. There he offered burnt offerings, grain offerings, and the fat parts of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was too small to hold them all.

decisions.choice: consecrated: made holy, set apart for sacrifice
decisions.reason: The central part of the courtyard was set apart so that it could be used like an altar for that day.

decisions.choice: the fat of the peace offerings: the part burned for Yahweh
decisions.reason: The fat of a peace offering belonged to Yahweh and was burned on the altar (Leviticus 3:3-5, 16).

decisions.choice: the bronze altar: the great altar of the courtyard
decisions.reason: 1 Kings does not describe it, but 2 Chronicles 4:1 says it was twenty cubits square. Even so it could not take so many offerings.

decisions.choice: them all (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable does not repeat the list of offerings a second time.

records.gloss: And held Solomon at the time the that the festival, and all Israel with him, an assembly great from [the] entrance of Hamath to [the] wadi of Egypt, before Yahweh our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days.
pieces: So at that time Solomon held the festival, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, for seven days and then seven more days, fourteen days in all.

L.65: And Solomon held the festival at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days.

R.65: So Solomon and all the people of Israel celebrated the festival at that time. A huge crowd came, from Lebo-hamath in the far north to the Wadi of Egypt in the far south. They celebrated in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God for seven days, and then for seven more days, fourteen days in all.

decisions.choice: from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt: from the far north to the far south
decisions.reason: These are the northern and southern limits of the land promised to Israel (Numbers 34:5, 8). Lebo-hamath means "the entrance of Hamath", and may be the name of a town on the way to Hamath in Syria. The Wadi of Egypt is the dry stream bed at the southwest edge of Canaan.

decisions.choice: seven days and seven days, fourteen days: the Hebrew is kept
decisions.reason: The Greek translation has only "seven days". The parallel in 2 Chronicles 7:8-10 explains the fourteen days: seven days for the dedication of the altar and seven days for the festival, followed by a closing assembly. The Hebrew of Kings agrees with that account.

decisions.choice: Yahweh our God: the writer counts himself among Israel
decisions.reason: Here the narrator speaks of "our God", joining himself to the people whose story he tells.

decisions.choice: the festival: the Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: Lebo-hamath
decisions.reason: Literal, Balanced and Readable give the place as one name. Readable adds where the two places lay.

records.source: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי֙ שִׁלַּ֣ח אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וַֽיְבָרֲכ֖וּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ לְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם שְׂמֵחִים֙ וְט֣וֹבֵי לֵ֔ב עַ֣ל כָּל־הַטּוֹבָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֣ד עַבְדּ֔וֹ וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: On the day the eighth he sent away the people, and they blessed the king and went to their tents joyful and good of heart for all the good that had done Yahweh for David his servant and for Israel his people.
pieces: On the eighth day he sent the people away. They blessed the king and went home, joyful and glad at heart for all the good {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for David {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant and for Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

L.66: On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king and went to their tents, joyful and good of heart for all the good that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for David {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave and for Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

R.66: On the eighth day he sent the people home. They thanked the king and wished him well, and went home happy. They were glad because of all the good things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done for David, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, and for Israel, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: the eighth day: the day after the seven days of the festival
decisions.reason: The Festival of Booths lasted seven days and was followed by a solemn gathering on the eighth day (Leviticus 23:36, 39). 2 Chronicles 7:9-10 says that the closing assembly was held on the eighth day and the people were sent home on the twenty-third day of the month.

decisions.choice: went to their tents: went home
decisions.reason: An old expression from the time when Israel lived in tents (12:16; 2 Samuel 20:1).

decisions.choice: blessed the king: thanked him and asked God's good for him
decisions.reason: The people return the king's blessing (verses 14, 55).

decisions.choice: went home; servant (Balanced, Readable); slave (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the idiom of the tents in plain words. David is Yahweh's "slave" at Literal and "servant" at the other levels, as in verse 24.
